beats.html:
To haunt a place
first meant to visit it often.

From Old French hanter,
to frequent.

The ghostly sense shows up
in Shakespeare, around 1590.
A ghost haunts a house

the way a regular
haunts a cafe.

beats.html:
A Minnesota town answered
Halloween pranks with a parade.

Soaped windows. Tipped outhouses.
Cows loose on Main Street.

In 1920 Anoka gave its kids
a parade, a bonfire
and bags of candy.
It has held it every year since,
except 1942 and 1943.

beats.html:
Your porch pumpkin's family
was farmed 10,000 years ago.

Seeds and rind were found
in a cave in Oaxaca, Mexico.

Farmed earlier
than maize or beans.
And yes, it is a fruit.
One of the oldest
farmed plants in the Americas.

beats.html:
Wartime Halloween ran on
popcorn balls and cider.

Sugar was among the first
groceries rationed
in World War II.

Newspapers printed
ration friendly recipes
before the holiday.
People kept the holiday
by changing what they baked.

beats.html:
Thriller was the first
music video the Library
of Congress kept.

It joined the National
Film Registry in 2009.

1 of 25 films
chosen that year
for preservation.
The graveyard dance
is officially history.

beats.html:
Most faces we see
in objects read as male.

Faces in outlets, clouds
and pumpkins have a name.
Face pareidolia.

In a study of 3,815 adults,
90% of these faces
were rated male.
The brain gives a pattern
a whole personality.
